title: Low-bandwidth prefetch + tool-bridge (PRD - WIP)
body:
Overview:
This sketch proposes a compact streaming + tool-bridge mode for the Hosted API focused on low-bandwidth clients (mobile apps, edge devices, intermittent connections). The core idea: deliver progressive, usable deltas while letting the server coordinate and, where allowed, proxy or federate lightweight tool calls (price lookups, calendar queries, micro-API adapters) via an explicit compact framing. The design trades some generality for small wire-size, easy resume semantics, and predictable client SDK ergonomics.

Why this exists (motivation):
- Many mobile workloads care about first usable bytes and network cost more than full fidelity.
- Tool calling increases round-trips; we can reduce client pain by letting Hosted API prefetch and/or act as a bridge for trusted microtools.
- Current streaming contracts assume stable high-bandwidth connections and large frames; they are awkward on poor mobile networks.

Goals:
1) Compact progressive frames that let clients render partial answers quickly (progressive summary, key facts, structured attachments).
2) Tool-bridge: optional server-coordinated tool calls that either return a boxed result or a small token for client to fetch.
3) SDK ergonomics: tiny client surface for mobile SDKs (iOS/Android/React Native) that hides resume/repair logic.
4) Backwards compatibility with existing streaming clients; negotiated via a small handshake.

Non-goals:
- Full replacement for existing verbose streaming surfaces. We keep those for high-bandwidth desktop/servers.
- Large binary attachments on the stream. Bridge can hand out short presigned URLs instead.

Personas:
- Mobile PM building an in-app assistant who wants 95% of value under 100KB mobile data.
- Platform engineer integrating third-party small tools (currency/price) with SLA and audit.
- SDK lead who must ship safe resume logic in 2 sprints.

Requirements (high-level):
- Protocol must support: partial text frames, structured objects, tool call frames, tool result frames, finalization/failure frames.
- Handshake indicates bandwidth_tier (low/medium/high) and bridge policy (none/proxy/deferred).
- Ability to checkpoint and resume a session by providing last-seen frame id.
- Observability hooks: per-frame latency, per-tool-call success/error, payload sizes.

API sketch (request):
{
  "model": "redwood-compact-v1",
  "input": "Summarize and get the latest price for TSLA",
  "stream": true,
  "bandwidth_hint": "low",
  "bridge_policy": "proxy_if_allowed",
  "prefetch_hints": ["price:ticker"]
}

Streaming framing (NDJSON-like compact lines):
- frame-type: partial | tool_call | tool_result | url_hint | final | checkpoint | error
- minimal wire fields (type, id, body) to keep bytes small.

Example frames (client sees):
{"type":"partial","id":"f1","body":"Summary: Tesla reported strong delivery numbers..."}
{"type":"tool_call","id":"tc1","tool":"price-bridge","payload":"{\"ticker\":\"TSLA\"}"}
{"type":"tool_result","id":"tc1","result":"{\"price\":189.42}"}
{"type":"final","id":"f2","body":"Final: summary + price included"}

Notes on tool_call/tool_result semantics:
- tool_call frames are issued by the model or server. If bridge_policy allows, Hosted API will either: (a) proxy the request to a registered internal/external tool and return tool_result inline; or (b) emit a token/url_hint that the client can use to fetch result later.
- tool_result must be small (JSON) or else return url_hint to a presigned artifact.
- All bridged actions must be recorded in audit logs (for Private/Dedicated customers) and respect KMS/HSM policies.

Security and privacy: 
- Bridge mode is opt-in per-API key. By default, hosted-api will not proxy external tools for untrusted keys.
- Tool payloads can be scrubbed; we must offer a redact=opt parameter in the handshake.

SDK ergonomics (mobile-first):
- Public surface: startSession(request) => stream listener object with callbacks:
  - onPartial(textOrDelta)
  - onStructured(obj)
  - onToolCall(callMeta) // if client must act or show pending UI
  - onToolResult(callId, smallResultOrHint)
  - onCheckpoint(token)
  - onFinal(finalBody)
  - onError(err)
- Resume: startSession can take resume_token to request frames after last checkpoint. SDK handles idempotency by acknowledging last frame id.
- Transport: HTTP/2 chunked or websocket. For very low bandwidth the SDK should default to chunked text over HTTP/1.1 with compressed frames.
- Size-sensitivity: SDK provides a bandwidth estimate hook so the server can compress or reduce fidelity.

Tool-bridge operational model (how to onboard a microtool):
1) Tool owner registers tool with policy (trusted clients, allowed customers, rate limits).
2) Hosted API stores metadata and optionally proxies per-customer credentials in a vault.
3) At runtime the model emits a tool_call with tool id. Hosted API checks policy, either proxies call or returns a short token.
4) Tool results recorded in trace and audit log.

Observability and telemetry:
- Per-frame size and latency, per-tool-call success rate, bridge proxy latency, and bytes-saved metrics (prefetch wins).
- Add a per-session SLI: first-usable-frame-time under 500ms for low-bandwidth 3G test harness.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0: internal alpha, server-only emulation with SDK stub, limited to redwood-internal accounts.
- Phase 1: beta for mobile customers, bridge_policy=deferred (no proxy), collect telemetry and adjust frame shapes.
- Phase 2: proxy bridge for trusted partners with narrow tool whitelist and per-tool SLAs.
- Phase 3: general availability with billing metrics for bridge proxy usage and bandwidth tiers.

Success metrics (first 9 months):
- 50% reduction in bytes transferred for targeted mobile workflows vs baseline.
- 80% of sessions see first partial within 700ms on simulated 3G.
- Tool-call latency (end-to-end) under 200ms for internal microtools in 90th percentile.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Exact compact encoding: NDJSON vs small binary CBOR. Tradeoffs: human readable vs smaller. TODO: perf eval by Eng-applied-ml team.
- Billing model for bridge proxy: per-call vs per-GB. Finance to propose.
- Auditing surface for Private customers: need legal review for proxied tool calls.
- Failure modes: if bridge fails mid-stream, should server emit a graceful fallback frame to let clients continue? (recommended: yes, emit tool_error then continue).

Next steps (immediate):
- Eng-serv-runtime: prototype compact framing + resume semantics (2 sprints).
- SDK lead: implement stub SDK with startSession + resume (1 sprint).
- Product: finalize bridge policy tiers and billing proposal with finance.
- Security & Compliance: initial review on proxied credentials and audit logs.

Notes to self / meeting prep:
- Bring a short demo for weekly API sync: show 3G device with bridge_policy=deferred and full proxy.
- Prepare microbench results for NDJSON vs zipped-CBOR for 50KB payload targets.

End of draft.

(If accepted, this will become the primary low-bandwidth streaming PRD and we will factor out the universal streaming doc into a compatibility appendix.)
